Rs. 1,010 million vs. Rs. 31.7 million: Minister reveals foreign travel costs of Ranil and AKD

cards.what_happened: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa told Parliament that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips during his 26 months in office. By comparison, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight foreign trips over a similar period.
details: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa shared the figures in Parliament on Saturday, November 21. He said former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips during his 26 months in office.

According to the minister, 421 people went with Wickremesinghe on those 33 trips. The trips stretched from his visit to the United Kingdom on September 17, 2022, to his visit to India on June 8, 2024.

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake made eight foreign trips in his first 26 months, costing Rs. 31.7 million in total. The minister added that the current President did not claim any extra or combined allowances for those visits.
key_facts: Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips in 26 months.
President Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight trips over a similar period.
Minister Nalinda Jayatissa revealed the figures in Parliament on November 21.
421 people accompanied Wickremesinghe on his 33 trips.
Wickremesinghe's trips ran from a UK visit on Sept 17, 2022 to an India visit on June 8, 2024.

cards.blurb: A minister told Parliament that Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on foreign trips, far more than President Dissanayake's Rs. 31.7 million.
cards.spoken: Here's a story about how much money two of Sri Lanka's leaders spent on trips abroad. A government minister, Nalinda Jayatissa, told Parliament that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent one billion and ten million rupees on thirty-three foreign trips during his twenty-six months in office. That's a lot of globe-trotting, and four hundred and twenty-one people went along with him. By comparison, the current President, Anura Kumara Dissanayake, spent just thirty-one point seven million rupees on eight trips over a similar stretch of time. The minister also pointed out that President Dissanayake didn't claim any extra or combined allowances for those journeys. So the numbers show a big gap between the two leaders' travel spending, and it's now on the public record in Parliament.

cards.what_happened: A 6.8 magnitude earthquake hit the Indian Ocean near Banda Aceh on Saturday (21). Sri Lanka’s Department of Meteorology said there is no tsunami threat to the island. The National Tsunami Early Warning Center said the quake happened at about 3:12 PM on November 21, 2026.
details: The earthquake was recorded at a depth of 156 kilometres. Its epicentre was at latitude 8.04° South and longitude 127.57° East. The National Tsunami Early Warning Center gave the time as approximately 3:12 PM on November 21, 2026.

After the quake, the Department of Meteorology issued a No Tsunami Threat Bulletin at 3:30 PM. The bulletin told people in coastal areas around Sri Lanka about the situation. It confirmed that the earthquake does not pose a tsunami threat to Sri Lanka.
The advisory was issued to keep coastal communities informed after the seismic event in the Indian Ocean. The report came from Newswire.

Parliamentary Committee reviews Sri Lanka’s tariff policies and trade agreements

cards.what_happened: The Committee on Ways and Means held discussions on Sri Lanka’s tariff policies and trade agreements. MP Vijesiri Basnayake chaired the meeting, and Acting Director General Somasena Mahadiulwewa briefed the committee.
details: The source is Newswire. The Committee on Ways and Means held discussions. The meeting discussed Sri Lanka’s tariff policies and the progress of ongoing bilateral and multilateral trade agreements.

The meeting was chaired by MP Vijesiri Basnayake. It focused on the current status of trade agreements and measures to advance negotiations. Acting Director General of the Department of Commerce, Somasena Mahadiulwewa, briefed the committee on the country’s trade policies and agreements.

The committee stressed the need to conduct feasibility studies on trade agreements currently under negotiation. It also wanted steps to ensure that discussions progress. Deputy Ministers Chathuranga Abeysinghe and Eranga Weeraratne, along with several MPs, attended the meeting.

world.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out

cards.what_happened: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, a Mexican drug lord on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, was arrested after a shoot-out with Mexican authorities. Special forces detained him and seven others in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, and the US is now seeking his extradition. Seven suspects and four Mexican army members were killed.
details: Mexican authorities have arrested Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, a drug lord on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, after a shoot-out. Mexico's defence secretariat said special forces detained him and seven other people in Guasave, in the state of Sinaloa, on Friday. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, and so were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave.

The secretariat said the forces used US intelligence on his whereabouts, moved in with what it called "stealth and surprise" and set a perimeter to stop him escaping and reinforcements arriving, but came under attack from gunfire and explosives before entering the property and arresting him. Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave, and people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds. Eight people were arrested in total, including his second-in-command, who is also his cousin, and his brother-in-law, the group's financial operator; a grenade launcher, other weapons, drugs and cash were seized, and while Meza Flores, his cousin and his brother-in-law were flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the other five remained in Sinaloa.

Meza Flores, who is 44, leads the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, and is thought to have been active in drug trafficking since the 1990s, evading authorities until now by keeping a relatively low profile. He was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, and was first charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 and charged again in 2019, accused of conspiring to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019. He was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to set up his own cartel by 2013, and his group has since fought what US officials called an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.

The FBI accuses him of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs", and the US is seeking his extradition. He was added to the bureau's most-wanted list in 2025, accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture, after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills seized in 2024; then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico. Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who made stemming the flow of drugs across the southern border a key election pledge, while Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on cartels to resist US intervention on Mexican soil, welcoming closer collaboration but resisting US boots on the ground. The US Consulate General in the city of Hermosillo said it was "monitoring reports of ongoing security operations, armed clashes, road blockades, and vehicle fires that occurred overnight in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave, and Navolato" after the arrest, and advised US citizens to stay alert for potential violence and residents to remain sheltered in place.
cards.why_it_matters: Mexico has stepped up its fight against drug-related crime after pressure from US President Donald Trump, and the arrest removes a man the FBI accuses of flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine and heroin; the US is now seeking his extradition.

FBI says he flooded the US with fentanyl, cocaine and heroin; US seeks extradition; first charged in 2012.
